# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*The following is Angular's official best-practices rules file, included verbatim from
<https://angular.dev/assets/context/best-practices.md>. It is part of the Angular
architecture.*

You are an expert in TypeScript, Angular, and scalable web application development. You write functional, maintainable, performant, and accessible code following Angular and TypeScript best practices.

## TypeScript Best Practices

- Use strict type checking
- Prefer type inference when the type is obvious
- Avoid the `any` type; use `unknown` when type is uncertain

## Angular Best Practices

- Always use standalone components over NgModules
- Must NOT set `standalone: true` inside Angular decorators. It's the default in Angular v20+.
- Do NOT set `changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` explicitly. `OnPush` is the default in Angular v22+.
- Use signals for state management
- Implement lazy loading for feature routes
- Do NOT use the `@HostBinding` and `@HostListener` decorators. Put host bindings inside the `host` object of the `@Component` or `@Directive` decorator instead
- Use `NgOptimizedImage` for all static images.
  - `NgOptimizedImage` does not work for inline base64 images.

## Accessibility Requirements

- It MUST pass all AXE checks.
- It MUST follow all WCAG AA minimums, including focus management, color contrast, and ARIA attributes.

### Components

- Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility
- Use `input()` and `output()` functions instead of decorators
- Use `model()` for two-way bound properties with `[(prop)]` syntax instead of pairing `input()` with `output()`
- Use `computed()` for derived state
- Use `linkedSignal()` for state derived from multiple reactive sources that must stay synchronized
- Prefer inline templates for small components
...

content.text: `RoleService.refuseViewer`/`refuseUnlessPermitted` are themselves `@Transactional`, so a refusal there marks the bulk-settle transaction rollback-only even though `bulkSettle` catches it. Fix:

input.command: cd /home/daniel/ui-work/runs/202610271-as/sandbox/officehq-angular-spring; f=src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/role/RoleService.java; sed -n 1,55p $f

cd /home/daniel/ui-work/runs/202610271-as/sandbox/officehq-angular-spring; f=src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/role/RoleService.java; python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/role/RoleService.java'
s=open(p).read()
for m in ["public void refuseUnlessPermitted","public void refuseViewer"]:
    s=s.replace("    @Transactional(readOnly = true)\n    "+m, "    // a refusal leaves the caller's transaction usable (a bulk action refuses one claim and goes on)\n    @Transactional(readOnly = true, noRollbackFor = ResponseStatusException.class)\n    "+m)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n "noRollbackFor" $f; timeout 590 bin/e2e > .run/e2e.out 2>&1; tail -30 .run/e2e.out

content.text:
The sheet's due-total and overdue-total are now trimmed, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. With three or more people's figures, the single highest and single lowest are left out. A due-total of n/a doesn't count as a figure; an overdue-total always does.

**The change itself:**
- **Screen** (`src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`): a new helper, `trimmedSum`, now produces the due-total and overdue-total. Those two values feed both the totals row and the header. Per-person figures, the per-grade and per-period totals, the overdue count and the claimed total are calculated as before.
- **TOTALS audit line** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/RollupService.java`): `dueTotal()` and `overdueTotal()` use the same rule, so the audit file matches what the screen shows. The ROLLUP lines and `claimed-total` are unchanged.

**A separate bug I had to fix:** one test failed at a bulk settle, and the cause was an existing bug unrelated to totals. When any selected claim was refused because of the user's role, the whole request failed with a server error ("Transaction silently rolled back"). So the screen showed an error instead of the settled/refused counts. The two refusal checks in `RoleService` (`refuseViewer` and `refuseUnlessPermitted`) run in their own transaction, and a refusal there cancelled the whole bulk action even though bulk settle catches it. I set them to leave the caller's transaction usable (`noRollbackFor = ResponseStatusException.class`). A refusal that isn't caught still rolls back everything, as before. This also affects any other place that catches these refusals.
